sn12.19:1.2: Ignorance is a cognitive defilement, craving an emotional defilement. Their pairing here shows that they work together, rather than being in a strict linear relationship as in the standard set of twelve links. Dependent origination is textually stated as a line, and pictorially as a circle. However in many ways, the best image is a spiral: circling around like a coiling snake or like DNA, never exactly repeating, but also never completely new. | The phrase “shrouded by ignorance” describes beings roaming through transmigration ([sn15.1](), [an3.76](), [iti14]()). _Nīvaraṇa_ ultimately stems from Vṛtra, the serpent who, by coiling around the mountain, both “shrouded” it in darkness, and “hindered” or blocked it. | The reading here is _sampayutta_ (“coupled”) rather than _saṁyojana_ (“fettered”) found elsewhere.
sn12.19:1.3: From the sequence of the sentence, it would appear that etesam va annaterena applies to “pleasure or pain”. However this idiom regularly takes the instrumental: see AN 4.170, AN 4.258, etc.
